description: tikr trading pipeline: iggy producers (ws ingest) and ClickHouse sinks with insert rates and latency histograms, plus the replicated iggy-server cluster (WAL, replication, drops, denials). Metrics scraped by the de-msa2 `tikr-k8s-pods` job and the `iggy-server-k8s` / `iggy-server-k8s-dev` jobs (namespaces tikr / tikr-dev).
title: tikr

panels.description: Total rows inserted per second into ClickHouse across all sinks.
panels.title: ClickHouse insert rate

panels.description: Messages consumed from iggy per second across all sinks.
panels.title: Sink consume rate

panels.description: WebSocket messages received per second across all producers (raw exchange ingest).
panels.title: Producer ingest rate

panels.description: p99 ClickHouse insert latency across sinks. High values (hundreds of ms) reflect the per-INSERT HTTP round-trip cost.
panels.title: CH insert p99

panels.description: Producer WS messages dropped + producer insert failures per second. Should be ~0.
panels.title: Drops & failures / s

panels.description: Rows inserted per second per sink (job) into ClickHouse.
panels.title: ClickHouse insert rate by sink

panels.description: Messages consumed from iggy per second per sink. Compare to producer ingest to spot consumer lag.
panels.title: Sink consume rate by sink

panels.description: iggy poll latency p99 per sink (time to fetch a batch from iggy-server).
panels.title: iggy poll latency p99 by sink

panels.description: ClickHouse insert latency percentiles (p50/p90/p99) aggregated across all CH sinks.
panels.title: ClickHouse insert latency percentiles

panels.description: ClickHouse insert latency distribution over time (heatmap of the histogram buckets). Reveals bimodality the percentile lines hide.
panels.title: ClickHouse insert latency heatmap

panels.description: WebSocket messages received per second per producer (job).
panels.title: Producer WS ingest rate by producer

panels.description: Producer iggy batch-send latency p99 per producer (time to publish a batch into iggy).
panels.title: Producer batch-send latency p99

panels.description: Producer WS messages dropped and insert failures per second per producer. Non-zero = data loss at ingest.
panels.title: Producer drops & insert failures

panels.description: Scraped iggy-server replicas of this namespace's VSR cluster (jobs `iggy-server-k8s` / `iggy-server-k8s-dev`). Both clusters run 3 replicas, so 2 is the quorum: orange = one replica down, red = no quorum and writes stop.
panels.title: Replicas up

panels.description: Clients connected across all replicas (producers, sinks, web console). The SDK follows the cluster metadata to the primary, so most clients sit on the primary.
panels.title: Connected clients

panels.description: Replicated prepares made durable per second by the fastest replica. Every replica persists every prepare, so the max (not the sum) is the cluster write rate.
panels.title: WAL prepares / s

panels.description: Highest per-replica `messages` gauge (total count of messages). See 'Messages stored by replica' for divergence between replicas.
panels.title: Messages stored

panels.description: Partition WAL writer failures plus frames shed instead of delivered (`frame_drops_total`, all variants). `or vector(0)` because iggy only exports a counter family after its first increment.
panels.title: WAL errors & frame drops / s

panels.description: Duplicate partition builds discarded plus parked frames rejected for a dead incarnation, over the dashboard range. iggy documents both as 'non-zero is a caught anomaly'.

targets.expr: round((sum(increase(partitions_duplicate_builds_discarded_total{namespace="$namespace", job=~"iggy-server-k8s.*"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(partition_frames_rejected_stale_total{namespace="$namespace", job=~"iggy-server-k8s.*"}[$__range])) or vector(0)))

panels.title: Caught anomalies (range)

panels.description: Scrape health per replica. The replica label comes from the pod name without the ReplicaSet hash, so a restarted pod continues the same series.
panels.title: Replica up

panels.description: Connected clients per replica. The primary holds most connections; a shift between replicas marks a view change (new primary).
panels.title: Connected clients by replica

panels.description: Prepares covered by completed partition WAL batches, per replica. All replicas should track each other; a replica below its peers is falling behind replication.
panels.title: WAL prepares / s by replica

panels.description: Group-commit efficiency: prepares per durable WAL batch (higher = fewer fsyncs per prepare). The dashed series count durable groups that took the optional pre-barrier wait.
panels.title: Prepares per WAL batch

panels.description: Active WAL bytes on disk, retained prepare bytes charged to the WAL budget, and bytes queued / in flight to the writer. Growing queued or in-flight bytes mean the disk cannot keep up.
panels.title: Partition WAL bytes by replica

panels.description: Committed entries (right axis) and their payload bytes (left axis) that each replica keeps to repair lagging peers.
panels.title: Repair ring by replica

panels.description: Per-replica `messages` gauge (total count of messages). A replica that stays below its peers has not caught up.
panels.title: Messages stored by replica

panels.description: Completed partition WAL checkpoints per second (left axis) and checkpoints waiting for storage completion (right axis). A pending count that keeps growing means storage is stalled.
panels.title: WAL checkpoints

panels.description: Frames shed instead of delivered, cluster-wide, by frame class (`variant`) and refusal reason. `full` = a shard inbox was full; `consensus` or `forward_replica_send` drops can stall replication.
panels.title: Frame drops by variant & reason

panels.description: Cluster-wide rates: replicated prepares a backup dropped as out of order (gap check), state transfers refused by the serving peer, metadata reads refused at the read frontier, parked frames for a future epoch, and repair serves deferred for a purge. Bursts are normal during a view change or rollout; a steady rate is not.
panels.title: Replication gaps & refusals

panels.description: Retryable denials sent to clients, cluster-wide: the client's request queue was full, a transient partition denial, or a consumer offset refused at the per-partition admission limit.
panels.title: Client request denials

panels.description: Cluster-wide rates of WAL writer failures, partition reconcile failures (retried), and the counters iggy documents as anomalies (duplicate builds, stale frames, stats decrements clamped at zero).
panels.title: Errors & caught anomalies

panels.description: Highest per-replica count of streams, topics, partitions, segments and users.
panels.title: Cluster objects

panels.description: Partitions materialised and removed by the reconciliation loop per second (left axis), and consumer offset keys whose file could not be loaded or unlinked (right axis, still counted against the admission limit).
panels.title: Partition reconciler
